answer: Reciprocal proximity scoring. Each agent gains standing only when it sits inside a persistent sparrow-like cluster: its neighbors must themselves name it as a neighbor, and the edge must survive repeated random audits. A global atlas of edge lifetimes flags pairs whose connections appear together and vanish together. An attacker must sustain genuine two-way traffic and latency across many kernel agents for weeks, paying real compute and bandwidth per fake node rather than a one-time fee.
